utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-32-T, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you able to hear us, sir, in that far away place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Domazet: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness VG87. To continue where we left off yesterday, you described Monday the 15th, the day you went into town and never returned to Pionirska Street. My question for you is the following: Do you know (redacted) ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you happen to see him on that particular morning when you left Pionirska, that is to say, Monday, the 15th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of your neighbours at all on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't meet any of my next-door neighbours. I saw a woman I knew and I asked her where her husband was, and she said that he wasn't at home. And I doubted that that was true, but I didn't see him, so I can't actually say whether he was at home or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I thought, yes. Yes, It seemed to me that he was carrying a bottle. Perhaps it wasn't, but that's what it looked like to me, and a megaphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're not getting a translation of the question in English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear now? Could counsel repeat his question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Apparently there was a breakdown somewhere. Would you repeat your question, please, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you were able to see Mr. Vasiljevic from time to time, you watched what he was doing from time to time, did he give the impression of an individual who might have been under the effects of alcohol to a greater or lesser extent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I wouldn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you can't say or --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he was. I would rather say he wasn't intoxicated than he was. Now, that all depends. Some people take to drink differently, but that wasn't the impression I gained. He wasn't attacking anybody, he wasn't rolling around or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. I didn't think that was the case. I know how you described his movements. But of course it would have been difficult to assess whether somebody was drunk or not, or tipsy. Did you happen to know (redacted) from Sase at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very slightly. I know that he was a tall man. He worked on the left bank of the Drina. I don't know for what company. We weren't friends, but I did know him a little. Not very close, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you happen to notice him on that particular day in Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just a few, Your Honour Re-examined by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 87, yesterday Mr. Domazet asked you a number of questions regarding the times that different events happened. Do you recall being asked questions regarding the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's see if I can -- perhaps I remember. Could you refresh my memory? What do you actually mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet asked you, for example, the time that you first smelled smoke. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. About 2000 hours, thereabouts, perhaps a little before that, but roundabout 2000 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he asked you several questions regarding times that different events happened concerning your wife. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I do, not only my wife but quite a few women together, several of them. There were four, plus a child, and then afterwards, when they went up there to take the car from the garage, I thought everything was over, but then between 8.00 or 2000 hours and 21 hours they came back again and they evicted people from the flats into that -- that is to say, that group of women, with one child and sent them off to the school. That was between 8.00 and 9.00. And they kept them there until 2300 hours, then took them back to Pionirska, took them down the street. I wasn't able to see or hear them any more, so that was my final parting with them. I didn't see them any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 87, my question to you is: Are these times that you have given us here yesterday and today, are these approximations of the times that you believe or are you certain that these are the times that these events occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: An approximation, because it was dark. Sometimes I would go to the place that I looked out from. I had a watch, or didn't. So I would say it was roundabout that time, in the space of 30 minutes at the most, not more than the space of 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified that you later learnt that your wife died in the fire on Pionirska Street that day, and my question to you is: Do you know from personal knowledge whether she was put into the house before the fire was started or sometime after the fire was started? Do you have any personal knowledge regarding that fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard from a man who escaped the fire when there was a detonation and explosion -- I don't know. There was an explosion of some kind and the door opened and the man jumped out of the fire. And this group was thrown inside together with my wife. I heard from him, and he was a distant relative of my wife. The man died two years ago in Sarajevo. He's not alive now. He's no longer living. So that was the first time that I heard about it. And later on in Medzedza, when I got there, I heard some more about it, five or six days later. I was in Medzedza for 20 days for treatment and there were stories going around. Some people said it wasn't, but according to what I think and what I heard, most probably she died in the fire. She was thrown, living, into the fire, into the flames, and you could hear screams at around 2000 hours and three hours later, 2300 hours or perhaps two and a half hours or two hours later, if they went -- no. Between 8.00 and 9.00. They stayed there until 2300 hours. Well, that's it. It's easy to calculate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're referring to hearing screams. Is this what was told to you or are you saying now that you did hear some screams on that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG87 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first burning there was a house which was burnt and smoke. I didn't hear any screams then. I just heard screams when they came back for the second time to the apartment where there were four women and children. They set up a great resistance. They entreated and pleaded, but it was all to no avail. They turned them out of the flat, into the direction of the school house. They kept them there until 2300 hours and when they came back after that I heard screams again and entreaties and pleadings that they could be allowed to go to Olovo and so on. So I heard screams on two occasions: When they expelled them and when they returned them from the school to Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 87. Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for giving your evidence. We are grateful to you for giving that evidence and you are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too. That's fine. It wasn't very long. It didn't take too long. That was short, short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps I should record our gratitude to the technical crew present at the remote location that we now are able to see the witness a little better than we were able to yesterday. It's a far better picture, even though we don't have the United Nations flag in the background. Have you got the next witness ready?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, madam, the Court deputy who is just beside you there will read to you the terms of the solemn declaration that you are required to make before you give your evidence. When she has read it to you, you should say in answer to my question do you make that solemn declaration, you should say yes. Would you please read the solemn declaration to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. Sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: May I proceed? I would ask that the witness be shown document 85, the pseudonym sheet. Perhaps the court deputy -- Your Honour, I think there's no other way to do this other than to go into private session and read this to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. We'll go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We are now in public session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 105, are you from the municipality of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, were you married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many children did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what village you were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Zlijeb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how many families are in that village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: I can't tell you. There were quite a lot, but I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of the people in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your family own and work a farm in your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992 did your husband leave your village because of security concerns?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: My husband worked in Sarajevo and he came back for us to take us out of that village, but he wasn't able to and he disappeared. He fled to Zepa and disappeared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did he flee to Zepa with? What members of your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: With my sons and the people from the village, the menfolk. They all fled to Zepa. Some of the women did too, but not all of them. Some of the women stayed on to look after the land and the cattle, but we weren't able to look after everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you remain behind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes. My mother-in-law was an invalid. I wasn't able to go with her anywhere, so I stayed until they came to expel us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a time that regular soldiers of the Yugoslav People's Army came to the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They did come, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they set up a command post approximately one half hour from your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: They came in a kombi van and we were told they were the White Eagles, but I don't know who was what. All I know is they came. They sent me into my house, one of them. He placed an automatic rifle to the nape of my neck and forced me into the house. He searched the house to see if there were any weapons hidden or whether anybody else was hidden in the house and then he left and I stayed in the house. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us approximately when that occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it was Ramadan or not. I'm not sure. I can't say for sure. I can't remember. It's ten years since that time. You know how it is. One forgets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did one of these soldiers identified to you as White Eagles show you a list of names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: No. They did show names, but not to us. They didn't read them out. They said, "You have a husband, you have sons." That's how it was. That's what they said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ask where your husband and where your sons were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they did. They did, and I said that my husband was in Sarajevo. I didn't dare say that he had left for Zepa. But what they had actually done was to flee to Zepa. And then he asked me where my sons were, and I said my sons were in Austria and that's true. Two of my sons actually were in Austria. Two of them came back to take us away from the war. However, they were not able to do so. They fell upon hard times, and two of them disappeared. One was killed, one is in Zepa, one disappeared, and my husband in Srebrenica too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: And my brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when these White Eagles searched your house for weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They did. I've already said. I've told the truth. I've told you how it was. Had a pistol but with a permit. And my brother-in-law had a pistol with a permit. They took them off -- they took them away with them when they left, so there was nothing left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention now to the Muslim holiday of Bajram. Do you remember when Bajram was in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes. I think -- whether it was June or July. It's after May. But you know, I'm illiterate, so I don't know these things. But on the third day of Bajram they came to expel us from our house. It was the third day of Bajram. And a Wednesday. I know that it was a Wednesday. There was Milojica from Pozdercici, and he said, "Collect what you need, take some bread for three days, and get going. You are to be ready." And they rounded us up at some customs places. I'm sorry. At Carine, at a place called Carine, and the elderly couldn't go there, so then we got some cattle and some bulls and helped us along and then they put us into a truck and took us to the fire brigade centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first time that the White Eagles came to your house, did you recognise any of the people that were among that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: No, I didn't. No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This second time that you're describing now on the third day of Bajram, did you recognise any of the people in this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Well, my neighbour Milojica from Pozdercici, he was a neighbour. He came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many people were involved in this second incident on the third day of Bajram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Well, quite a few of them, but I don't know. I was afraid. You know how it is when you have to leave your house and all your belongings and everything. I didn't count them. There were quite a few of them. That's the main thing. And they rounded us up in a meadow, in a field. They rounded us up there and then waited until we were all there, we had all gathered there. And then they put us all into a truck and took us to the fire brigade centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the truck for us? It was an army truck or a private truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: No, it was not a military truck, no. Just a regular truck, a privately owned truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where precisely did they bring you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: To the fire brigade centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that in the centre of Visegrad town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, in the centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many floors are in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Two floors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Court what occurred when you were brought to the fire brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: When we were brought to the fire brigade they rounded us up. They took our names down. They registered us. Then they told us to discard our gold, jewellery, and money, which we did, if we had any. We gave them everything. But they didn't trust us. They didn't believe us. And then they herded us all in a room upstairs, in groups of four, four women, and we were searched there again. And once again we had to give them everything we had. I had my wristwatch with me, but he took it away from me and he smashed it on the floor. And I said that that was the only thing I had. And then they took us back downstairs. At that point the men were taken away, one by one. And that's how it happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to a person as "he" who searched you and broke your watch. Do you know the identity of that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: I don't know his name, because I didn't know him, but I heard other people refer to him as Lakic by surname. But I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the course of that search, were you and the other women made to take your clothes off?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction. Lakic's son.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes. Some did, some didn't. I took some of my clothes and he searched me to see if I had any jewellery or money on me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the people at the fire brigade at this time, did you recognise any of the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: The people who took our people away? Lukic and Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you about Milan Lukic first. Did you know him prior to this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, that was a very leading question and it doesn't help us. If you want to get an identity, please get it from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the circumstances under which you learnt the name of this person you just described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can describe him. People who knew Lukic and this other guy, Vasiljevic, people knew him. I cannot tell you anything else. I can only tell you what I know about. I can only tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what you know about this other person you're referring to as Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Only what I know. They took away Mujo Gluscevic and his daughter was there when he was taken away, and she started to cry. And he took her. He hugged her. He said, "Don't cry." I also have a daughter. Your daddy will be back, will be exchanged." That's all I know about Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I ask you what Mr. Vasiljevic did, I would ask you to describe the circumstances under which you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We didn't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: He used to work as a waiter. That's what I heard from other people, that is, that he was from Blaca, from that area. That's what I heard. And that's all I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the name of his wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Esma. His wife is from Pozdercici, from the village of Hrastovi. I think her name is Milojka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Court when is the first time you saw Mitar Vasiljevic at any time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Here we go again. That is a leading question. There is no suggestion that there is any evidence of that name. Don't you understand, Mr. Groome, that if you want this case to be accepted, it should be presented in the usual way, non-leading? Leading questions invite an answer which are of very little value. You are destroying your own case by continually doing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. It's not my intention to use the first name and it's my intention to simply establish when is the first time she saw the person she referred to in her testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: As Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As Vasiljevic. I apologise for using the first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us when is the first time you saw this person you've referred to as Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: I don't know what else to say. I didn't know who he was until I saw him at the fire brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were asked to look at a group of pictures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you recognise any of the people in those pictures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Only Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you mark the picture that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Well, because I used to see him, but I didn't know who he was. But I did see him in Visegrad from time to time, and then I saw him at the fire brigade. So that was the picture that I had, the image, I mean, at the fire brigade centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw this group of pictures, did you do anything to document or indicate which picture you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes. I pointed to his photograph and I said that that was the man that I knew, that I recognised him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I show the witness the next witness, I'd ask that we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How is her pointing to it or otherwise marking it going to identify her?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think when she is shown the exhibit and the Court sees the exhibit it will be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when some of the men that were in the fire brigade were taken from the fire brigade? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: You're asking me? Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when some of the men were taken from the fire brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: You mean at what time or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: They were taken at dusk. It was already dark when they were taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: One by one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days transpired between the day that you arrived at the fire brigade and the day that the first man was taken out of the fire brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: On the third day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were the people that took these men out of the fire brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: The Lukics and this other man, those who were with us, who came with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these men taken out at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they taken out on the same day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: On the same day, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the identities of the people that were taken out of the fire brigade on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: The names? Let me see. There was Sabanovic. Just a second. Mustafa. Ibrahim Kesmer, Hamed Kesmer, Meho Softic, Samir Softic, Hasan Gluscevic, Hasib Gluscevic, Mujo Gluscevic, Sifet Gluscevic, Sejo Hodzic, Adem Kosic, Salko Suceska, Djelal Hodzic, Avdija Nuhanovic, Huso or Husein Vilic, Meho Agic, Emin Agic. I think that's 18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you specifically about one of these people. You mentioned Mujo Gluscevic. Did you observe him when he was taken out of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were the people that took him out of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: The two of them, Lukic and Vasiljevic. Nobody else came. The two of them would come from time to time to the fire brigade, no one else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mujo Gluscevic, did he have other family members present in the fire brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: His mother, his wife, two children, his son and his daughter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how old was his daughter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: I think she was not older than 12 or 13, but I don't know for sure. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time her father was taken away, did either of these two people you've described as taking them away, did they say anything to this girl?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Vasiljevic said something, because she was crying, and then he took her, he put her in his lap, and he said, "Don't cry. Your daddy will be exchanged at Pale."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were present when that conversation --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: But never, you know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were present when that conversation took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you kept in the fire brigade building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: I can't remember whether it was five, six, or seven days, thereabouts. I don't remember. Because we were afraid at that time, and ten years have gone by, so you know how it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a day when you were taken out of the fire brigade building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: There were convoys that had been organised beforehand for us to be taken to Olovo, and when we left the fire brigade, we were first of all rounded up, those from the village of Zlijeb. They didn't let us board the trucks and they took us back to the fire brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were put on a truck that left the fire brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Later on we were put on a truck and taken to Lijeska, but once we got to Lijeska, the truck broke down and we spent there the whole day. And after the truck was repaired, it was taken back to Visegrad. They said that we would be taken back to Visegrad, to the SUP building, and they said, "Then let the SUP people do with them as they please."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were brought back, where were you housed at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: In the school building, in Nova Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many days did you spend in the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Three or four days, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 105. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Will you be able to find out for us, Mr. Groome, just when Ramadan was in 1992, perhaps also when Bajram was? Unless there's some other evidence about Bajram. There may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have an official document from the Muslim society with the calendar for that year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Domazet. Cross-examined by Mr. Domazet:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, you testified today that on the third day of Bajram, certain individuals came to your village and told you to leave the village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to say what you have testified about today, did you ever give a statement to an investigator of the OTP here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember saying that the event took place on the 17th of June, 1992, on a Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it still your testimony that the event took place on Wednesday, on the 17th of June, 1992, that that was the date when you were taken to the fire brigade in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us today that they started taking people away on the third day after your arrival in the fire brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us that you spent five, six, or maybe seven days in the fire brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time, that is, during those five, six, or seven days that you spent in the fire brigade, did you also happen to see an individual whom you've referred to by Vasiljevic, apart from Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes. The two of them were the only ones who visited us there. No one else came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, but I should like to know whether the two of them visited you until the last day you were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: You mean in the school? They did while we were in the fire brigade but not when we were in the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I was asking you about the fire brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The two of them would come from time to time, just the two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe for us what they were wearing when they came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Civilian clothes. Civilian suits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything else, anything in particular that you would have noticed in connection with their attire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified today that you used to see the person that you identified as Vasiljevic in Visegrad but that you didn't know who he was until you saw him in the fire brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you who he was while you were in the fire brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes. All those who knew him told us that, because we were not that many there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was from other persons who were in the fire brigade that you heard that the person who came to see you with Lukic was Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You lived in the village of Zlijeb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often, how many times a year, would you go to the town of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Not many times. I went there very rarely, maybe two times a year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, when, if at all, did you hear about Vasiljevic's arrest and transfer to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: I heard that he had been transferred from the papers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was somebody else who showed you the paper? Because you are illiterate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone show you the paper with an article about Vasiljevic's arrest and transfer to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that paper that you saw, was there a photograph of him as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also happen to see the event on TV, either his arrest or his transfer to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, only once, because I don't watch TV very often, but I did see that once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw Vasiljevic on TV once when he was already in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that occasion that you said you saw Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: It was after his arrest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long after his arrest was it? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: No, I don't. It was a Saturday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, madam, I'm not asking you about the day of the week. It's very difficult to remember that. I would just like to know whether this was a month, two months, or three months after his arrest.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: No. No. Maybe one week after that that I saw him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, it's after 11.00. We'll go back to the usual timetable. We'll adjourn now until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, can you describe those two men for us, the ones who were the only ones to come to visit you during the time you were at the fire brigade, and you said that they were Lukic and Vasiljevic. Their height, perhaps, their build, and any other characteristic features that you might have noticed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Well, you're asking a lot of me. Lukic was taller, taller than Vasiljevic. Vasiljevic seemed to be shorter. I can't quite describe this to you. You know, I was very much afraid. You know how it is in times like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did either of those two people have a moustache or a beard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Vasiljevic had a moustache.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you note any other characteristic traits that could help us on the two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you only remember that the person you said was -- you named as Vasiljevic had a moustache; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He had a moustache.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mentioned Vasiljevic's wife, did you ever meet her or did you only hear about her from others, from other people who told you about her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: I would see her around. We weren't too far away from each other. I used to see her as a young girl, because the village is a small one. But when she married him, I didn't see her any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was in Visegrad, did you see his wife in Visegrad, and who told you that she was his wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: No. No. I didn't see her in Visegrad. I used to know her and see her around while she was an unmarried young girl, but later on I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the village of Kragujevac near your own village, the village in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we say that the distance isn't greater than one kilometre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts. Perhaps a kilometre, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the villagers, the natives of that village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes. I knew them all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give any other statement except the statement you gave to the investigator of The Hague Tribunal about these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the only statement that you made about the events of which you were an eyewitness you gave to the investigator of The Hague Tribunal; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when you gave the statement? Because not much time has gone by since.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, not much time has gone by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember a part of your statement, the following part of your statement, and is it true and correct when you said that when you were shown an album with 12 photographs, a photo array with 12 photographs, that in the statement to the investigator you said the following: "I think that I could recognise --" Just wait for me to finish, please, witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: I am listening to you. I'm listening to everything you're saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. "I think that I could recognise Mitar Vasiljevic if I were to see him again. You have shown me a series of 12 photographs marked with numbers ranging from 1 to 12. Picture number 3 seems to me to be someone I know. I think he is from Kragujevac, but I do not remember his name." Do you remember having given a statement of that kind to the investigator and when he showed you the photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. He had a moustache when he was at the fire brigade and then I couldn't actually -- but I remember seeing him and I remember saying all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did say that to the investigator of The Hague Tribunal; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that you thought the person was from the village of Kragujevac --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- did you have in mind a particular person from the village whom you said you knew well, because you said you knew the people from the village very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Well, no. I didn't have anyone in mind, but I do know the people from Kragujevac, and I thought, well, perhaps he might have been in Kragujevac. That's just what came to my mind. But I can't say that he's from Kragujevac. I didn't know where he was from when the person who came to the fire brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. But from your statement, it is clear that the person which you indicated on picture number 3 that you thought you recognised, you didn't say that it was actually Vasiljevic, whom you mentioned several times in your statement. You mention a man with the surname of Vasiljevic several times in the statement before that. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG105
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions for you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, madam, very much for giving evidence. We're grateful to you for the evidence you've given. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Whilst we're waiting for the other witness, Mr. Groome, I've seen the memorandum of service in relation to the subpoenas that you sought. Have you seen them yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, I haven't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think that the conditions that they seek to lay down may be a little difficult for the Tribunal to provide, but you better have a look at them, and when you have, we'll discuss them again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, madam, we want you to take a solemn declaration. The court officer there will show you on a card the terms of the declaration which you should make.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. [Witness testifies via videolink].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. Sit down, pleas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that the pseudonym sheet for this witness be placed in front of the witness at this time and I'd ask that it be marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The pseudonym sheet for Witness VG101 will be Exhibit P86 and it will be under seal. Examined by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness 101.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to sit back and relax. I'm just going to ask you some questions. I'd ask you to look at the sheet in front of you. Is that your name on the top line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the second line, is that your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the purposes of concealing your identity, we will refer to you as Witness 101, and I would ask you, if you need to refer to any of the other people listed on that sheet, please use their number. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. I've been told that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 101, where are you from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: I am from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what particular village?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The last two words from inaudible.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court what your educational background is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: A caterer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's the highest level of schooling that you attended?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Secondary school, secondary school for catering.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you please tell us your ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: A Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention back to 1992. Can you tell us, without mentioning their names, who were you living with at the time in Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: I lived with my sister, my mother, two brothers, and their two children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to look at your sheet in front of you. Is the witness number VG78 your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did your family operate a small farm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, they did have one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Court approximately how many houses are in this village of Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: About 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how many people all together lived in the village of Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number. There were quite a few, but not all of us were there at the time we left for Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Court the ethnic mix of the Koritnik community?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. It was a mixed village. There were Serb houses and Muslim houses as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the spring of 1992, were there any problems between the Muslims and the Serbs living in Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Well, yes, there were some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: You mean before, at the beginning of the war, or before?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war began, were there problems between the Muslim population and the Serb population of Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No. No. Not before, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to the 13th of June, 1992. Do you recall that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, I can. A neighbour from the neighbouring village of Loznica came. His name was Radomir Grujic. And he said we had to leave the village and that we should come to a place called Greben on the 14th of June, that a bus would come to us, that we shouldn't be afraid and that someone of the Muslim nationality would be with us and that we should go to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Radomir Grujic before this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Mr. Grujic alone or with other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: He came alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he give you a reason for why you had to leave your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Well, he said we had to, that the Serbs from the village of Prelovo were exerting pressure on them and that they said that they would search our houses and that they couldn't guarantee our safety if we stayed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Grujic tell you where you were going to be taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He said we were being taken to Kladanj, in a convoy, that there would be a number of buses, at least six buses in the convoy, and that we were going to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time was Kladanj considered a town in Muslim territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you stated that you were told to go to a place called Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Greben. Where is Greben in relation to your village, Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Well, Greben -- you can reach Greben in a half an hour's walk. It is on the road to Visegrad. That's where the bus station was, in Greben. It's a half hour's walk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 14th of June, did you walk to the village of Greben?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. We started out from the village early so that we could be in Greben by 8.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how many people left the village of Koritnik that morning on the way to Greben?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: About 42. I think that's how many we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us what was the ethnic mix of this group of 42 people that left Koritnik on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: They were all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it your understanding that Mr. Grujic's instruction applied to all people of Koritnik or just the Muslims of Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Just the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you left the village, did the Serb people of Koritnik remain behind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us approximately what time you set out from Koritnik for the village of Greben?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: I think we set out at about 7.00 so that we should be there at exactly 8.00, to arrive before the buses did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did there come a time when you did arrive at Greben?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see a bus there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had Mr. Grujic said that he would come to Greben as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, he did, but he wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the village of Greben?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but we stayed there a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did a bus ever come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No. No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 101, I'm going to ask you to describe for the Court if a person were to walk from Koritnik to Visegrad, could you please tell us the villages they would pass through in the order that they would pass through those villages, beginning from Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that. You pass through Srpsko Selo, Koritnik, Greben, Sase, Kosovo Polje, Kalate, and then you come to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to repeat the name of the place above Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Sase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you left the village of Greben?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. We were there for a long time and then a neighbour, a Serb, his name was Milorad, he was from Greben. I think he was nicknamed Micun. And he stood around with us for a time and then he said that he didn't dare stand there any more and that we should go, because the buses probably wouldn't arrive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he suggest to you where you should go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: To go to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go in the direction of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: We were there for a little while longer and then my neighbour, Ilija Gavrilovic and Radomir Grujic went before us, went to Visegrad ahead of us, with a relative of mine, and his father, rather. And then they came back and they said, "Come on, you Turks. You come to where you should go."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this Radomir Grujic that you're mentioning now, is he the person who initially told you you had to leave Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No. No. He was a younger man. Dragomir. Dragomir Grujic. And Radomir Djuric. Radomir Djuric told us we had to leave the village, and this was Dragomir Grujic. They were two different people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of this second person that you're mentioning now, Dragomir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: He's a Serb, but he lived in Dalmacija for a time, so that's why he came to visit his father. His parents were divorced, so he lived for a time with his mother in Dalmacija and then he came to live with his father in Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also mentioned the name Ilija Gavrilovic. What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Also a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us precisely what did these two men do in relation to the group of people from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly did these two men do when they met with the group of Koritnik -- the group of people from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: They got out of the car and said, "You Turks all go to where you have to go." Then they switched on the motor and went to Koritnik again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the car that these two men were driving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whose car did you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: It was a car belonging to one of my relatives from the village. It was a red --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't catch the name of the car.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Volkswagen. A red Volkswagen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to describe: The group from Koritnik, can you describe what the composition of the group was as far as the age of the group and whether they were men and women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: There were both men and women there, young women, girls, children. There was even a three-day-old baby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whose baby that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: It was the baby from a woman from the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know her name? Do you recall her name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do. Her name was Sadeta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the group from Koritnik, were they carrying anything as they walked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. We had a lot of things with us, and that's why we were slow. We couldn't move on very fast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what types of things the people were carrying and how they carried them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Well, mostly we had our clothes and our suitcases. Some people carried other things as well, like dishes and stuff like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you left Koritnik, did you believe that you would ever return to Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. That's what our neighbours guaranteed to us, the neighbours who came to us. They said that they would look after our belongings and that they would be back very soon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn why it was that the bus never came to the village of Greben?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: When we arrived in the village of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: -- a Serb from the village of Kalate told us that the bus had indeed started but that it broke down somewhere near Banja, so it was not possible for the bus to reach us. It was out of order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to repeat the name of the village that you said at the beginning of your answer. The interpreters missed it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Haluge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as you left Greben, what would be the next village that you would come to on the way down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Sase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the way down to Sase did you ever see any buses on the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did it take you to go from Greben to Sase?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: It's nearby, maybe a half hour on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do when you arrived in Sase?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: We stayed there for quite some time and then Spahic, this Serb man, told us that we should go to Visegrad as soon as possible, that he would go ahead of us to guarantee our safety in a car. So he left sometime before we did, but we never saw him again

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you left Sase, did any other people join this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, from the village of Sase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how many people from the village of Sase joined the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Five. Five new people came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to approximate the time of day that it is when you leave Sase for Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No. I don't remember the exact time. But we stayed there for quite a while. That is where we stayed longest, in Greben and in Sase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, walking from Sase to Visegrad, would you have passed through the village of Kosovo Polje? Did you hear my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There was a break in the transmission. You could see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you walked from Sase to Visegrad, did you pass through the village of Kosovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your way down to Visegrad, did you at any time see a bus on the road that you were walking on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: A bus from Centrotrans carrying a large number of people probably from the village of Vlahovici passed us on the way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "Centrotrans," is that the name of a bus company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, a bus company, a transport company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anybody on this bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you later learn that there was a person from Koritnik on this bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. She stayed behind after we left. She was quite old. She couldn't leave. Then they put her on the bus and she was on this bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you also learn where she was brought on that bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. She was first in Kladanj, then in Visoko, later on in Sarajevo, and she died two years ago of natural causes, in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time when this group did eventually reach Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know exactly what time it was, but we did reach Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the first place that you went in Visegrad when you got to the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: As we entered the town, we were met by some Serb policemen who were standing in front of the SUP building. They were shouting at us. And they told us to continue down the street towards the new hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by the SUP building, do you mean the police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The police were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the entire group go with you to the police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No. We didn't actually go to the SUP. We went to the new hotel, to the area outside the new hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the entire group go to this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the new hotel in relation to the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: It is next to the old bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know the name of this new hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: That's how it was referred to, the new hotel, Novi Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe to us precisely where you were in relation in to the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: In front of the hotel, at the entrance to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you describe for the Court what is in the front of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: There was a taxi stand opposite the entrance of the hotel, and we were standing there, between the taxi stand and the hotel. We stayed there for a while and after some time we moved to the garden of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is the garden of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Near the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe, aside from this group -- I'm sorry. I interrupted you. Do you want to repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from the group from Koritnik and from Sase, were there other people on the street at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did something happen while you were standing by the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: We were lined up there, two by two. They singled out three or four men and told them to go to a nearby village, and they were told that some people were killed there and their bodies had to be buried, that they were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you describe who you're referring to when you say "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Those police officers, the ones who had lined us up. They selected some men and told them to go to the village of Nezvci, where there were some killed Muslims whose bodies had to be buried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many policemen were present at that time, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Three or four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from these -- these policemen, do you know what their ethnicity was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other people of Serb ethnicity in the area where you were in front of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many, but there were a lot of people there who were coming in and out of this hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of these people armed with weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. All of them were armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe generally the dress of these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Some wore camouflage uniforms and some wore the former JNA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when somebody arrived in a car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. While we were standing in that garden we were being verbally abused and mistreated. They argued about where we should be sent to. Then a car came and stopped near the garden and Mitar Vasiljevic came out of the car and he told them to release us, to let us go, and that we should go to Pionirska Street, where there were some empty houses, to Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this person you're referring to as Mitar Vasiljevic alone or with other people in the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: I only saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had you seen this person at other times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to describe for the Court how it was you knew this person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: I didn't know him personally, but I knew him by sight. When I was a child, when I was in the elementary school, people knew Mitar as an alcoholic, and that is how we children used to see him. He would pass by. But then there were many other people who knew him very well while he was working as a waiter in Visegrad, so I knew that it was him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you first knew of him in elementary school. Are you able to approximate for us approximately how many years you knew him at the time that you saw him this day in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Many years, because we went to school in Prelovo and he's from the area of Prelovo, from a village whose name I don't know. So he would pass by. He would pass through Prelovo and we would see him when we went to school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise him immediately on this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time in March of this year that you were asked to view a set of photographs by an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you recognise any of those photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, I recognised Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask that we go into private session briefly to -- I'd ask that that exhibit be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 101, I would ask you to describe as best you remember what was this person, what was Mitar Vasiljevic wearing on this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: He was wearing a former Yugoslav People's Army uniform and a large black hat on his head and a black raincoat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything covering or disguising his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to tell us again what it was he said, but please use the words that he said as precisely as you're able.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: He said that we should go to the Mahala settlement, to Pionirska Street, to abandoned Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier that some of the people, other people in the area, were shouting insults to the group. I'd ask you to describe what it was that they said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: They called us balijas. They cursed us, mentioning Alija, our state, telling us where are now Murat and Avdija to defend you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there Serb police officers present at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there paramilitaries there as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to describe as best you're able the car that Mitar Vasiljevic arrived in in front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No. I don't know what car it was. I didn't see the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This place that Mr. Vasiljevic instructed you to go, were you familiar with this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how are you familiar with this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: I knew the area because my relatives lived there. They had houses there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how frequently would you visit this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Not very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you left the new hotel and went in the direction of Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how much time transpired between the time Mr. Vasiljevic instructed you to go to Pionirska Street and the time you actually left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: We left immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Vasiljevic say anything else to you regarding going to Pionirska Street at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the entire group go to Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you approximate the distance for the Court between the New Hotel and Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but it took us about 15 minutes to get there on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that the group was still carrying its bags and belongings that it had carried from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we still had everything with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the first place that you went -- I'll withdraw that. When you arrived at Pionirska Street, where is the first place that you went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: We stood on the street for a while. We didn't know where to go. While we were standing there, Mitar came to us. There were quite a few of us. We needed maybe two or three houses. But he rounded us up and he told us to go to one and single house and to be there, all of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did he arrive at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: By car. He came immediately after us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, using the words that he used, what it was he said to you and the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. He said that we should go to Kladanj, that we could no longer live together and that once in Kladanj we should select the houses as the houses in our area and that we -- that it would take us six hours to get to Kladanj, that no one would harm us, and he gave some kind of certificate for our safety to one of the men, that should we -- should the police control us, that we should show them our identity cards and that we should not be afraid, that nobody would do us any harm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he direct you to a specific house on Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He told us to enter one particular house there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know the name of the owner of that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: No. I think that his name was Ragib, but I didn't know the person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the school on Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe where the house was that you were directed to go to in relation to the school on Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
utterances.text: The school was on the right and the house was further down, on the left side, almost at the very beginning of the street, Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you go to the house that you were directed to go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG101
